Operational scoring criteria: Data obtained from at least two institutionally independent healthcare organizations, without shared patient pools, with at least four reported baseline characteristics: age, sex, histological type, and tumor location.
Single-institution or clinically restricted cohort, with at least two core characteristics, including histological type and tumor location, reported.
Highly restricted data source, substantially underreported cohort characteristics, or insufficient information to assess cohort composition.
At least 300 unique patients across the development and evaluation cohorts, without double-counting patients across data partitions.
100-299 unique patients.
Fewer than 100 unique patients; only image-, slice-, or patch-level counts without a verifiable patient count; or patient-level sample size not reported or verifiable.
Institutionally independent external validation with verified patient-level separation. Mixed designs qualify only when the independent external component is separately identifiable and verifiable.
Internal hold-out, cross-validation, or temporal validation with documented patient-level separation; or mixed designs with a qualifying internal component but an unverifiable external component.
Image-, slice-, or patch-level random splitting without patient-level separation; identified data leakage; or insufficiently described validation procedures.

All three conditions are satisfied: (1) publicly accessible complete training and inference source code; (2) publicly accessible final trained model weights; and (3) reported key training parameters, including optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and random seed.

Partial implementation resources are available, or methodological descriptions provide sufficient details on model architecture, data preprocessing, and training procedures to support independent implementation.
Neither usable implementation resources nor sufficient methodological details are available to support independent implementation.
Established clinical task, appropriate task-specific reference standard, and at least one clinically meaningful subgroup evaluation reporting model performance or behavior.
Clinically interpretable task and appropriate task-specific reference standard, but no clinically meaningful performance-based subgroup evaluation.
Simplified or self-defined objective without established clinical interpretation; inappropriate or inadequately defined reference standard; or insufficient evidence of clinical relevance.
At least two distinct types of substantive additional analyses, including at least one ablation or systematic error/failure analysis, together with another complementary analysis.

At least one substantive additional analysis, such as ablation, error/failure analysis, robustness testing, calibration, sensitivity analysis, or a controlled physician comparison, without meeting the criteria for 2 points.
Primary performance metrics and routine model comparisons only, without substantive supplementary experimental investigation.
Equal weighting across six domains.
Higher appraisal category.
Moderate appraisal category.
Lower appraisal category.

Each domain was scored on a three-level ordinal scale (0-2), yielding a maximum total score of 12. Sample size was based on unique patients rather than images or derived samples. Institutionally independent data sources required distinct patient recruitment and non-overlapping cohorts; different campuses or branches of the same healthcare organization were not considered independent unless this independence could be verified. Reference standards were assessed according to the investigated task. Histopathological confirmation was considered appropriate for tumor diagnosis and classification, whereas expert annotations or consensus could serve as reference standards for segmentation. Subgroup analyses had to report model performance or behavior across clinically meaningful groups; descriptive cohort characteristics alone were insufficient. Analyses used to support clinical relevance were not counted again for analytical depth unless independently designed. A score of 0 was additionally annotated as M (criterion not met) or U (unreported or unverifiable). The overall categories represent descriptive levels of methodological rigor within this review-specific framework and are not validated thresholds of clinical validity or risk of bias.
